title: Privileged Access Recertification Playbook (Quarterly) - Draft
content:
Purpose:
This playbook defines the operational steps and automation patterns for quarterly least-privilege recertification and privileged access audits. It covers RBAC v2 role-to-actor mapping checks, audit-log schema validation, SIEM export queries for evidence collection, and the mechanics of evidence automation uploads.

Scope:
- All privileged roles defined in RBAC v2 (admin, infra-ops, model-onboard, customer-support-priv, dedicated-admin)
- All orgs and teams using Shared Drives, Dedicated, and Private deployments where human access or service principals have elevated permissions
- Quarterly cadence (default) and on-demand recertification after major org changes (mergers, infra migration)

Owner & Participants:
- Playbook owner: Ariana Chen (Security & Compliance)
- Reviewers: Team leads for infra, serving-runtime, private-deployments
- Evidence automation: Infra-eng (Dylan Brooks), SRE (Liam O'Connor)
- Approvers: Head of Security (Priya Patel)

High-level timeline (quarterly):
1) T-21 days: Automation run to generate candidate list and evidence bundles (RBAC diff + last 90d audit logs)
2) T-14 days: Notify reviewers with per-role recert tasks (Jira tickets auto-created)
3) T-0 to T+7 days: Review window (7 days) — reviewers complete cert or request justification
4) T+10 days: Escalation/appeal resolution
5) T+14 days: Finalize changes (revoke or retain) and ship infra changes via IaC PRs

Criteria for recertification decisions:
- No privileged activity in last 90 days -> flag for least-privilege justification or revoke
- Activity restricted to documented and approved maintenance windows -> retain with note
- Role assigned to terminated users or stale service accounts -> immediate revoke and create incident ticket
- Temporary elevated access > 30 days -> require remediation plan and manager sign-off

RBAC v2 checks (examples to run):
- Role enumeration: export roles and bindings via /internal/rbac/v2/export endpoint (json). Verify no wildcard namespace bindings.
- Sensitive permissions list: {cluster_admin, model_deploy:write, billing:modify, keys:unwrap} (run intersection against each role).
- Orphaned bindings: bindings where principal not in identity directory (okta/azuread).
- Service account vs human principal: ensure service accounts have documented justification and rotation policy.

Sample RBAC diff command (infra automation):
- curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/internal/rbac/v2/export?format=json > rbac_snapshot_$(date +%F).json
- python tools/rbac_diff.py --base snapshots/rbac_snapshot_Q1.json --head rbac_snapshot_today.json --out diffs/qX_rbac_diff.json

Audit log schema & mapping (for evidence):
- Required fields we export to SIEM: timestamp, event_id, actor_id, actor_type (user|service), action, resource_type, resource_id, request_id, success, ip_address, user_agent, policy_decision, kv_cache_hit, model_version
- Preferred canonical field names (SIEM-friendly): @timestamp, event.id, user.id, user.type, event.action, resource.type, resource.id, network.ip, http.user_agent, outcome
- Retention note: privileged_access events need 1 year cold storage and 90 days hot in SIEM for quick queries.

SIEM export & queries (Splunk/Datadog example snippets):
- Export path: s3://redwood-evidence/privileged-recert/YYYY-MM-DD/<org>/evidence.json.gz (encrypted with KMS: projects/redwood/key-evidence)
- Splunk query to list all privilege grants in last 90d: index=redwood_logs sourcetype=privileged_access action=grant OR action=assign_role | stats count by user.id, role, action, _time
- Datadog log query for unresolved revocations: sources:redwood AND event.action:revoke AND status:failed | sort @timestamp desc | limit 100

Evidence automation design:
- Worker (lambda/k8s job) runs on schedule: 21 days before quarter end, collects: RBAC snapshot, recent audit logs (90d), active token list, list of active service principals, last login times from IdP.
- Package into evidence bundle: metadata.json (manifest), rbac.json, audit_logs.ndjson.gz, idp_users.csv, sas_keys.csv. Sign bundle with internal GPG key and upload to S3 evidence path.
- Create Jira ticket per role with bundle URL; auto-assign to role owner.

Minimal evidence manifest (manifest file fields we require):
- manifest.id (uuid), manifest.generated_at (ISO8601), manifest.snapshot_period (start_iso/end_iso), manifest.sources (list), manifest.signer (email), manifest.signature (base64)

Automation pseudocode (sketch):
- schedule: quarterly_cron("0 4 1 1/3 *")
- steps:
  1) fetch_rbac() -> rbac.json
  2) fetch_audit_logs(since=90d) -> audit.ndjson.gz
  3) fetch_idp_users() -> idp_users.csv
  4) assemble_manifest() -> manifest.json
  5) sign_and_upload(bundle) -> s3://redwood-evidence/...
  6) create_jira_tasks(bundle_url, per_role_list)

Reviewer checklist (what reviewer MUST verify):
- Is the role still needed? (if yes, why)
- Did the principal perform privileged actions in the snapshot window? If not, request justification or revoke.
- Is there an active, documented business justification and manager approval?
- Are service accounts rotated and pinned to an owner in the owner column?
- Is MFA enforced for human principals with write-level or higher privileges?
- Any temporary approvals open longer than 30 days? Escalate.

Escalation & enforcement:
- T+7 days no response: auto-escalate to manager + cc security@redwood.ai
- T+10 days unresolved: create remediation ticket assigned to infra-eng and mark role as 'restricted' in RBAC (deny by default).
- Immediate revoke if evidence of abuse or account compromise (follow Incident Response  playbook).

Quality checks for automation (pre-deploy test plan):
- End-to-end run in staging with single org; validate manifests and signature verification; validate S3 lifecycle; validate Jira ticket creation in dev project; validate SIEM queries return expected events for seeded test users.
- Drift detection: once automation runs, run a second validation pass after 24 hours to ensure revocation PRs created and applied.

Operational runbook notes (quick commands):
- Manually generate evidence bundle: make bundle && ./tools/sign_bundle.sh bundle.tar.gz
- Verify signature: ./tools/verify_signature.py --file bundle.tar.gz --keyring keys/gpg_public.pem
- Re-run SIEM query for failed uploads: python tools/splunk_retry.py --query "index=redwood_logs ..." --since 90d

Open questions & TODOs (for next review):
- Should we reduce review window to 5 days for infra-critical roles? Pros/cons listed below.
- Add a one-click recertify flow in Console (product story, product-hosted-api).
- Map RBAC v2 permission codes to natural language descriptions for non-technical reviewers.

Appendix: sample SIEM queries (copy/paste friendly)
- Splunk: index=redwood_logs sourcetype=privileged_access action=(grant OR assign_role OR revoke) | table _time event.id user.id user.type action role resource.id outcome
- Elastic/Opensearch: POST /_search?q=event.action:(grant OR assign_role OR revoke) AND event.timestamp:[now-90d TO now]

Notes to self (informal):
- Need to coordinate with IdP team for last_login API (Priya to intro).
- Confirm retention costs with finance for 1 year cold S3 storage.
- Ask product if Console can surface 'my outstanding recert tasks' widget.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-15 initial draft by Ariana Chen
- 2026-01-12 added SIEM queries and schema fields (Dylan Brooks)
- 2026-03-10 expanded automation pseudocode and manifest fields (Liam O'Connor)
